stages.label: 1481 Paris Missale Parisiense
stages.scope: Identified book witness and the Eucharistic components supported by the cited original leaves or edition-identified contents index; no complete reconstructed missal.
stages.summary: The 1481 Paris-use missal has a checked original colophon and bounded Maundy Thursday folios. Neither a first composition date for those prayers nor a predecessor relationship follows.

evidence.locus: Original scan PDF pp. 155–156, fol. lxix recto–verso, and p. 494 colophon; Usuarium book 79 contents pp. 152–180
evidence.claim: Original folios identify bounded Maundy Thursday prayer/rubric material; the colophon dates the Dupré and Huym printing to 22 September 1481.

stages.limitations: The scan and selected leaves do not certify full physical or textual completeness; 1685, 1705 and 1738 originals are uncollated. GW M24596 cites a published dating study (Baurmeister 1999) under "Zur Datierung"; it has not been read, so the colophon year is kept as printed and flagged.
stages.reception: The local-use designation identifies the intended book tradition; actual adoption by every church and any continuing-use interval have not been established.

evidence.locus: Book 663 title and identity lines 11–23; contents pp. 1, 15, 127–165, 273–470

stages.label: 1496 Missale Cameracense, Higman for de Campis
stages.date_label: Penultimate day of February 1495 by the colophon (old style; 1496 new style)
stages.scope: One Paris print for Cambrai use; colophon and January calendar inspected.
stages.summary: The colophon states that this missal according to the use of the church of Cambrai was printed at Paris by Johann Higman at the expense of Johannes de Campis, with that church's customs and observances added, completed on the penultimate day of February 1495. The calendar carries Cambrai entries with folio references.
stages.limitations: The colophon year 1495 is old style (the Paris year then began at Easter), so the penultimate day of February 1495 falls in February 1496 by modern reckoning; GW gives 27/28 February 1495/96. The 1496 bounds express this conversion only, not a period of use. Not compared with the 1507 Lyon-held print, which was unavailable.
stages.reception: A manuscript note records purchase by an abbot named Gerard; diocesan use is not dated.

stages.label: 1738 Missale Parisiense, BnF B-178
stages.scope: Identified Paris-use missal edition and scholarly described Maundy Thursday postcommunion 1060; no original 1738 prayer body or whole-book text has been checked.
stages.witness_label: Missale Parisiense, 1738, BnF B-178; Usuarium book 7371
stages.summary: The exact BnF holding and year are catalogued. Ward discusses postcommunion 1060 in the 1738 Paris missal, while O’Connor’s MP annotation points to earlier Paris missals; neither establishes first introduction in 1738.

evidence.locus: Usuarium book 7371, identity fields: title, origin, age, shelfmark and Amiet 747
evidence.claim: Identifies a 1738 Paris missal edition and BnF B-178 holding.
Identifies the Maundy Thursday postcommunion as no. 1060 in the edited 1738 Paris missal.

evidence.locus: Annotated orations, entry 1060 and abbreviation MP
evidence.claim: The aggregate MP source mark points to Paris missals of 1685 and 1705, leaving the first introduction unresolved.

stages.limitations: The original Gallica scan linked from Usuarium returned 403 in the earlier inventory research; the 1738 original and 1685/1705 comparators are uncollated. No prayer wording is transcribed here, no 1481-to-1738 revision is asserted, and the catalogue year is not an effective-use date.
stages.reception: Publication and later scholarly identification do not establish adoption in every Paris church, a first-use date or continued observance.

evidence.locus: Usuarium book 7090, identity fields: original title, origin, age, BM Lyon 20390 and Amiet 1364; Amiet catalogue row 1364 for books 7090 and 7461
evidence.claim: Identifies the 1728 Rouen missal witness and exposes a possible duplicate catalogue row.

stages.limitations: No original 1728 book pages or paired 1495 text have been inspected. The book cannot establish a substantive reform, direct ancestry, text inheritance or actual diocesan uptake. Usuarium 7090 and 7461 may be duplicate descriptions; the physical relationship remains unresolved.
stages.reception: The Rouen designation is bibliographic; local approval, first use and parish reception have not been demonstrated.
